newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Oct base money slows to 13.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Oct base money slows to 13.5 pct.

text.p: The Philippines base money, a measure of domestic liquidity, slowed to a year-on-year growth of 13.5 percent in October from 15.3 percent in September, the Central Bank reported on Tuesday.
In a statement, Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson attributed the slower growth in money supply to the Central Bank's active open market operations.
He said the healthy cash position of the national government made it easier for the Central Bank to manage money supply.
To secure the continued deceleration of consumer prices, Singson vowed to sustain monetary discipline.

"We have reason to be more optimistic that the 6.5 percent year-end inflation can be met; it can even be better," Singson said, following news that October turned out a better-than-expected inflation of 4.7 percent.
Year-on-year growth of reserve money, a main determinant of base money, likewise slackened to 14 percent in October from 15.9 the previous month, the Central Bank said.
The latest preliminary data on both reserve and base money show these were nearly 20 billion pesos below set ceilings under the programme with the International Monetary Fund, it added.
